target_customer: Finance and accounting teams at large organizations (the site names Amazon, Mastercard and UPS as customers); originally e-commerce merchants and product teams buying integrations as Alloy Automation
problem: Finance teams spend heavy manual effort on the month-end close; Kinter sells AI accountants that run close tasks inside existing ERPs with human approval. As Alloy Automation, the problem was connecting e-commerce tools without the cost of enterprise integration platforms.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription (Alloy: $200 to $1,000+ per month per TechCrunch 2021; Kinter pricing not found)
product_category: AI accounting agents (formerly integration and automation platform)

founders.name: Gregg Mojica
founders.role: CTO of Alloy Automation, now CEO of Kinter
founders.background_notes: Started coding at 10 and worked professionally from 17 per his YC launch post.

founders.name: Sara Du
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2021-02-02) and a16z Series A coverage name her as co-founder and CEO. The Kinter YC page lists only Mojica; whether Du is still involved in Kinter was not found.

competitors.name: Zapier
competitors.what: Simple no-code workflow automation that Du found too simple

competitors.name: MuleSoft
competitors.what: Enterprise integration platform that Du called very expensive

technical_complexity.rationale: Alloy needed many third-party API connectors and reliable workflow execution, standard but broad integration engineering for a team of three engineers in 2020.

defensibility.rationale: Integration catalogs create some lock-in, but the founder later said integration infrastructure was becoming commoditized, which is why the team pivoted.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The a16z Series A coverage (2022) contrasted Alloy's neutral model with Shopify first-party tools; by 2025 Mojica said the integration layer was commoditizing and moved to AI accounting.

market_need_then: Shopify and BigCommerce merchants wanted automations between SMS, fulfillment and other tools and found Zapier too simple and MuleSoft too expensive (TechCrunch, 2021-02-02).

branding.domain_note: Current domain kinter.ai; earlier brand Alloy Automation. Date of the domain change not found.

identity.visual_style: Clean B2B software site with investor logos
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident enterprise AI tagline 'A new kind of power for finance teams'

rebrands.why: Mojica's launch post says the team left the commoditizing integration business and pivoted to AI accountants; one profile dates the finance positioning to 2025-11 (single source)

brand_strength.rationale: Alloy had a 2019 Product Hunt launch and press coverage, but the Kinter brand is new and no source shows brand-driven growth.

pivots.from: Broad automation tools, then e-commerce automation (Alloy Automation)
pivots.to: Integration platform for product teams (universal API)
pivots.why: E-commerce demand from Shopify and BigCommerce users led the first focus (TechCrunch 2021); the later move to integrations is described in secondary sources only

pivots.to: Kinter AI accountants for finance teams
pivots.why: Mojica says integration infrastructure was becoming commoditized (YC launch post)

outcome_analysis: Alloy Automation raised a $4M seed in October 2020 at a $20M post-money valuation led by Bain Capital Ventures and Abstract, then a $20M Series A from a16z in February 2022. Seeing integrations commoditize, Mojica pivoted the company into Kinter, selling AI accountants to finance teams, and the site names Amazon, Mastercard and UPS as customers. The pivot is recent, so its payoff is not yet established.
notes: Kinter is the later name of Alloy Automation (YC W20); the YC page describes Kinter and credits Mojica with building Alloy. The pre-seed $1M date is not stated; Bain says its pre-seed fundraise began March 2020. TechCrunch says $5M across two rounds; Bain labels its case study Seed; the a16z piece says seed early 2021 whereas TechCrunch says October 2020, and October 2020 is used. An aggregator lists a 2026-06 seed for Kinter with a16z, YC and Bain; this single aggregator claim is unverified and not recorded as a round. Competitor sources are dated February 2021, about 11 months after the batch, but describe the positioning at founding. A profile gives total funding about $27M, unverified.
